_README: M14 sleep-architecture atlas. Measured thalamic/cortical kinetics that SET the sleep rhythms, plus the measured sleep observables (band targets + relational facts) with citations and pre-stated tolerances. VP-SPEC C0-C4: nothing here is tuned to a target -- the spindle FREQUENCY is set by the cited T-current de-inactivation recovery, the waxing-waning ENVELOPE emerges from the cited Ca-mediated Ih upregulation, and the slow oscillation is set by the cited cortical slow-adaptation recovery. The same R19 cubic-bistable primitive and the M9 ephaptic ring/kernel (measured kappa) are reused; ZERO new tuning constants. Reproducing a sleep rhythm is NOT a claim about consciousness or experience.
units: tau in milliseconds; frequencies in Hz; drive/gain dimensionless (R19 substrate units).

t_current_deinactivation_recovery_tau_ms.role: SETS the spindle CARRIER frequency (slow recovery variable w of the TC relaxation oscillator).
t_current_deinactivation_recovery_tau_ms.source: Huguenard & McCormick 1992, J Neurophysiol 68:1373 -- recovery from inactivation of the low-threshold T-type Ca2+ current in thalamocortical relay neurons (depolarised range).

tc_active_membrane_tau_ms.role: fast membrane time constant of the active (high-conductance) thalamocortical cell.
tc_active_membrane_tau_ms.source: Destexhe, Rudolph & Pare 2003, Nat Rev Neurosci 4:739 -- short effective membrane time constant in the high-conductance in-vivo state.

ca_ih_upregulation_tau_ms.role: slow Ca-mediated Ih upregulation that TERMINATES each spindle and sets the inter-spindle refractory period -> the defining waxing-waning envelope.
ca_ih_upregulation_tau_ms.source: Luthi & McCormick 1998, Neuron 20:553 -- periodicity of thalamic synchronized oscillations via Ca2+-mediated upregulation of Ih.

slow_adaptation_recovery_tau_ms.role: recovery of activity-dependent adaptation (Na/Ca-dependent K+ current and synaptic depression) that SETS the <1 Hz Up/Down cycle.
slow_adaptation_recovery_tau_ms.source: Sanchez-Vives & McCormick 2000, Nat Neurosci 3:1027; Compte et al. 2003, J Neurophysiol 89:2707 -- cellular/network mechanisms of the slow (<1 Hz) oscillation.

nrem2_operating_point.role: tonic depolarising level of the TC-TRN recruitment loop that places the thalamus in the NREM-2 window where spindles occur. Sets WHETHER spindles occur and their repetition rate (reported as emergent), NOT the spindle frequency.
nrem2_operating_point.source: Steriade, McCormick & Sejnowski 1993, Science 262:679 -- thalamocortical oscillations across the sleep/aroused continuum; spindles occur in a specific membrane-polarisation window.

sleep_spindle_hz.gate: canonical peak in [11,16] AND >= 0.875 of the 8-seed robustness sweep in-band
sleep_spindle_hz.source: De Gennaro & Ferrara 2003, Sleep Med Rev 7:423 -- NREM-2 sleep spindles, waxing-waning 11-16 Hz.

slow_oscillation_hz.gate: canonical dominant low-frequency peak < 1 Hz AND >= 0.875 of the 8-seed sweep < 1 Hz
slow_oscillation_hz.source: Steriade, Nunez & Amzica 1993, J Neurosci 13:3252 -- novel slow (<1 Hz) oscillation of neocortical neurons (Up/Down states).

spindle_waxing_waning.gate: canonical envelope amplitude-modulation depth > 0.5 AND > 0.5 on >= 0.875 of the 8-seed sweep
spindle_waxing_waning.source: De Gennaro & Ferrara 2003, Sleep Med Rev 7:423 -- the characteristic waxing-and-waning amplitude envelope is the defining signature of a sleep spindle.

nrem_rem_band_shift.measured_direction: REM marker (theta+gamma) over NREM marker (delta+spindle) is HIGHER in the REM state than in the NREM state
nrem_rem_band_shift.gate: canonical shift index REM > NREM AND direction holds on >= 0.875 of the 8-seed sweep
nrem_rem_band_shift.source: Steriade & McCarley, sleep neurophysiology -- REM EEG is activated/desynchronized (theta+gamma dominant) whereas NREM is delta/spindle dominant.

dream_recall_mechanism.note: REM theta-gamma coupling drives hippocampal pattern completion (M2 Hippocampus). This honors the M12 observable dream_recall_theta_increase (already MATCHED in M12) via an actual mechanism and the M13 MI->recall pattern; it is reported as a mechanism, NOT scored as a new observable (de-duplicated).
dream_recall_mechanism.source: Hippocampal theta-gamma coupling and memory reactivation in REM (theta-dependent recall); reuses M2 Hebbian attractor recall.
